title: Canada Freezes Parents and Grandparents Sponsorship Intake, Leaving Thousands of Indian Families in Limbo
excerpt: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada has paused all new applications under the Parents and Grandparents Program as of July 15, processing only 15,000 existing files. Indian families — the largest user group — are pushed toward the costly Super Visa as their only option.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • IRCC has paused all new Parents and Grandparents Program applications as of July 15, 2026.
  • Only up to 15,000 previously submitted applications will be processed throughout 2026.
  • India is the largest source country under PGP, with over 34% of invitations.
  • The Super Visa is now the primary alternative but offers no permanent status or healthcare.
  • Processing times for existing PGP applications already stretch 24-48 months.
Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has formally paused the intake of all new applications under the Parents and Grandparents Program (PGP) as of July 15, 2026, according to an [update from immigration law firm Fragomen](https://www.fragomen.com/insights/canada-permanent-residence-sponsorship-applications-under-the-parents-and-grandparents-program-pause-update.html). The government will process only up to 15,000 permanent residence applications that were already submitted under the program during 2026. The freeze, first signalled in Ministerial Instructions issued in late 2025, effectively shuts down the main pathway for Canadian citizens and permanent residents to bring their parents and grandparents to the country on a permanent basis. ## Why It Matters for Indian Families India is the single largest source country under the PGP. In 2024-25, more than 34% of all invitations to apply were issued to Indian-origin sponsors, according to [VisaHQ's analysis](https://www.visahq.com/discussion/blog/canada-freezes-parent-and-grandparent-sponsorships-for-2026-leaves-indian-families-dependent-on-super-visa). The pause disrupts settlement plans for thousands of Indian permanent residents who were counting on reuniting with aging parents. Processing times for existing applications already stretch between 24 and 48 months. With the freeze potentially pushing first-application opportunities into 2027 or beyond, many families face years of separation with no clear timeline for resolution. ## The Super Visa Alternative Ottawa continues to promote the Super Visa as the primary alternative. The multiple-entry permit allows parents and grandparents to stay in Canada for up to five years per visit and is renewable while in the country. However, [immigration experts note](https://www.immigration.ca/what-are-the-options-for-bringing-parents-and-grandparents-to-canada-in-2026/) significant limitations that make it a poor substitute for permanent sponsorship: - **No work authorisation.** Super Visa holders cannot work in Canada. - **No healthcare access.** Holders are barred from provincial health coverage in most provinces. - **Mandatory private insurance.** Medical insurance costs approximately CAD 1,000 per year and must meet IRCC thresholds. - **Temporary status only.** It provides no pathway to permanent residence. For many Indian families, particularly those supporting elderly parents with chronic health conditions, these limitations create a heavy financial and emotional burden. ## Behind the Freeze The government says the pause is necessary to manage application backlogs and align with reduced permanent resident targets in the 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan. Canada has been progressively tightening immigration pathways over the past year, with the PGP freeze being one of several measures aimed at controlling intake volumes. IRCC confirmed that no new invitations to apply will be issued in 2026. Applications already submitted in 2025 — drawn from the 2020 Interest to Sponsor pool — are the only files being processed. ## What Families Can Do Immigration practitioners recommend that affected families consider the Super Visa as an immediate stopgap while monitoring IRCC for any updated instructions. Those who submitted interest-to-sponsor forms in 2020 but were not invited should keep their information current in case the program reopens in 2027. Humanitarian and compassionate requests will not be considered if IRCC does not accept the associated application for processing, further narrowing options for urgent cases. The freeze underscores a growing tension in Canadian immigration policy between managing volumes and maintaining family reunification — a pillar that has historically made Canada an attractive destination for Indian professionals and their families.
